name: Select
summary: Lets people choose one option from a list that opens on demand.
description: A select shows the current choice in a closed box and opens a list of options when activated; the browser or the platform renders the list, its keyboard interaction and its announcements. It fits a choice among many known values (a country, a time zone, a sort order) where showing every option at once would take too much room. Two to about six options worth reading side by side are a Radio group; a list of actions is a Dropdown.

anatomy.description: Root. Stacks the label, the control, the description and the message; carries the size and the forced state.
Text naming the field. Provides the accessible name; activating it focuses the control.
Box holding the control and the chevron drawn over its end edge.
The native select, drawn by the component as a closed box showing the chosen option. Receives focus, holds the value; the browser opens and renders the list.
Chevron glyph of the icon font at the end edge of the control, saying that it opens a list. Hidden from assistive technology, which learns it from the role.
One choice in the list, rendered by the browser: the component gives it no style of its own.

properties.name: Label
properties.description: Text of the option, what people read and what is announced.

properties.name: Value
properties.description: Value submitted when the option is chosen. Defaults to the option's position.

properties.name: Selected
properties.description: Whether this option is the current choice.

properties.name: Disabled
properties.description: The option stays in the list, dimmed, and cannot be chosen.

anatomy.description: Optional help text under the control (format, example, consequence), associated with it as its description.
Text saying what the severity means (what is wrong and how to fix it, what to check, what was confirmed), associated with the control as a description. Shown only with a severity.

properties.name: Size
properties.description: Control height, inline padding and text size scale together; the label, the description and the message take the field family's sizes per size (Forms rule anatomy).

options.description: Dense forms, toolbars, table rows (32 px high).
Prominent, single fields: a search page, a sign-in form (48 px).

properties.name: Label
properties.description: What the field asks for, as a noun phrase (Email address). Always visible.

properties.name: Placeholder
properties.description: Text shown while no option is chosen (Choose a country). A disabled, unselectable first option: never the label.

properties.name: Description
properties.description: Help text: expected format, example, or what the value is used for.

properties.name: Message
properties.description: What the severity means: what is wrong and how to fix it, what to check, or what was confirmed. Shown with a severity, in the color of that severity, and replaces errorMessage.

properties.name: Required
properties.description: The field must be filled to submit the form.

properties.name: Severity
properties.description: What the check of the value found. Replaces the invalid boolean: error, warning and success are the three severities of a form control (decision forms-severity); information that holds before any check is the description's job.

options.description: No severity: nothing was checked, or there is nothing to say (default).

The value is not accepted: the control takes the subtle error fill and the error border, the message says what is wrong and how to fix it, and the control is exposed as in error (aria-invalid on the web).
The value is accepted but deserves attention: the control takes the subtle warning fill and the warning border, and the message says what to check. No web state: said in the message text.
The value was checked and confirmed: the control takes the subtle success fill and the success border, and the message says what was confirmed. No web state: said in the message text.

properties.name: Disabled
properties.description: Non-interactive and skipped by the keyboard; the value stays visible. A select has no read-only state.

states.description: Resting: an outlined box on the default surface.
Pointer over the control. The box takes the surface hover tint, unless it shows a severity, whose fill stays; the border does not change. Needs a pointing device: touch has no hover.
Keyboard focus on the control. Shows the shared focus ring outside its border; pointer focus shows none.
Severity error: the control takes the subtle error fill and the error border, and the message is shown under the control, in the error color.
Severity warning: the control takes the subtle warning fill and the warning border, and the message is shown under the control, in the warning color. No web state beyond the data attribute.
Severity success: the control takes the subtle success fill and the success border, and the message is shown under the control, in the success color. No web state beyond the data attribute.
Non-interactive. Box, value, label and description drop to the shared disabled colors; hover and focus do not apply.

notes: Label, control, description and message stack, separated by container.gap; the control fills the width of the component, which the layout sizes.
Inline padding, minimum height and text size come from the size option; the corner radius and the border width do not change.
The chevron sits over the end edge of the control, which reserves room for it with padding-inline-end.

name.text: Computed from the label, associated with the control as its label element on the web. The description and the message are exposed as the accessible description, not as part of the name.

keyboard.action: Moves focus to the control. A disabled control is not focusable and is skipped.
Open the list and move through the options the way the platform's native select does; the browser owns this interaction.

guidelines.text: Expose the combobox role, the name, the value and the required, disabled and error states through the platform's native select, so assistive technology receives them without extra work.

Use the native select element rendered as a drop-down box: it exposes the combobox role, its value and states, and the browser owns the list, its keyboard interaction and its announcements. The list is not styled by the component.
Use a pop-up button to present a flat list of mutually exclusive options or states.
The chevron is decorative and hidden from assistive technology with aria-hidden="true": an icon-font glyph is written as its ligature name, which would otherwise be read with the value.

Label, value, description and message text contrast at least 4.5:1 with their background in every color mode and enabled state: label and value 19.03:1 (light) and 11.28:1 (dark) on the default surface, description 12.78:1 and 8.86:1, placeholder 6.08:1 and 6.40:1, message text in its severity color: error 6.12:1 and 7.06:1, warning 6.49:1 and 11.17:1, success 7.87:1 and 7.89:1 (on every surface level the lowest are error 5.79:1 in light mode and 5.30:1 in dark mode, warning 6.16:1 and 8.38:1, success 7.44:1 and 5.92:1). On the severity fills the value reads 16.91:1 (error), 17.15:1 (warning) and 17.31:1 (success) in light mode, 11.68:1, 11.55:1 and 11.43:1 in dark mode. Disabled text is inactive and exempt.

The border is what identifies the field, so it contrasts at least 3:1 with the adjacent surface in every color mode: 12.78:1 (light) and 11.28:1 (dark) on the default surface at rest, 12.09:1 and 10.33:1 on the hover tint; the severity borders (the accent functional border): error 6.12:1 and 4.97:1, warning 6.49:1 and 8.09:1, success 7.87:1 and 6.08:1 on the default surface, and at least 5.79:1 and 3.73:1 (error), 6.16:1 and 6.07:1 (warning), 7.44:1 and 4.57:1 (success) on every surface level; the focus ring 5.77:1 and 12.76:1. Disabled is exempt. Against the fill of its severity each border keeps it: error 5.46:1 (light) and 5.14:1 (dark), warning 5.87:1 and 8.28:1, success 7.18:1 and 6.17:1.
A visible focus indicator appears when the control receives focus, drawn outside its border.
The focus ring is drawn with :focus-visible, so pointer focus on the closed control shows no ring.
Every size is a pointer target of at least 24 x 24 CSS pixels through its minimum height: 32, 40 and 48 pixels.
A disabled select leaves the focus order; a disabled option stays in the list, announced as dimmed, and cannot be chosen.
Apple recommends a hit region of at least 44 x 44 pt; the small and medium sizes (32 and 40 pt) fall under it on iOS today: the Figma library has no platform heights.

Android recommends a touch target of at least 48 x 48 dp; the small and medium sizes (32 and 40 dp) fall under it on Android today. Expose an error with the error semantics so the message is announced with the field.
Color transitions of the control are removed when the user asks for reduced motion.

guidelines: The label is a noun phrase naming the choice: Country, Time zone, Sort by. Sentence case, no colon, no trailing punctuation.
Option labels are short and parallel; order them logically (alphabetical for long lists, most common first for short ones).
The placeholder, when any, is an invitation to choose (Choose a country), shown until a choice is made; it is never a valid value.
The message of an error says what to do, relying on the label it sits under: Choose one

examples.name: Medium, with a choice and a description
Medium, required and error
examples.description: No choice made in a required field; the message says what to do.

decisions.text: A Select with a severity is filled with the subtle functional background of its severity, control.background.error, .warning and .success (= form.control.background.<severity>, global.bg.subtle.functional.<severity>.default: #FEECEA, #FFF1C7, #DBFAE6 in light mode, #2B0B08, #1F1504, #011C16 in dark mode), at rest and on hover alike, under its severity border; the value, the placeholder and the indicator keep their colors; the disabled fill wins over a severity. It follows the Forms decision forms-severity-fill ("A control with a severity is filled with the subtle functional background of its severity … at rest and on hover alike, under its accent functional border").
decisions.rationale: Applied in #105 step 12 (spec and docs fixes) from forms-severity-fill, decided by the team in #103 step 12 point 1 (error) and step 13 point 1 (warning and success), the Text field family as the reference rendering. Measured: the value 16.91 to 17.31:1 in light mode and 11.43 to 11.68:1 in dark mode on the three fills, the tertiary text 5.43:1 at the lowest; the border on its fill 5.14:1 at the lowest.

decisions.text: The Select's component tokens alias the Forms family (form.*) wherever their value is the family's default: the container gap, the label's color and font sizes, the control's fill at rest and on hover, its border in each severity and its value, the description's and the message's colors and font sizes. No value changes. Overrides, kept until this component's own refinement: its border at rest stays global.border.accent.neutral.default, where the family has the field family's global.border.base.neutral.5. Disabled colors, geometry and checked colors stay its own.
decisions.rationale: Follows the Forms foundation's decision forms-token-family (#105 step 2b, point b6, decided by the team on 2026-11-27): the default decisions for a form control rely on form.* tokens, which a control can override for specific use cases.

decisions.text: The label, the description and the message take the field family's text sizes per size (small, medium and large): the label 14 / 16 / 16 px (medium, tight line height), the description 12 / 12 / 14 px, the message 14 / 16 / 16 px (medium). Before, all three were 14 px at every size. Option labels and option descriptions keep their sizes. A default, which this component's own refinement may revisit.
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-26 (#105 step 2b, point b4, option A as recommended); it follows the Forms foundation's decision forms-text-sizes. The team's words: "We choose A but we'll probably refine them properly when we'll tackle the Select, Checkbox Group, etc. form controls."

decisions.text: The label, the control, the description and the message are 6 px apart (container.gap = space.6, was space.4), as in the Text field family, following the Forms foundation (forms-part-gaps). The same value on every platform.
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-26 (#105 step 10, point 5, option D, proposed by the team, its three assumed values confirmed: "Yes, D as assumed, and deduce what's expected for the other platforms"). It follows the Forms foundation's decision forms-part-gaps. The Select was the one field at 4 px.

decisions.text: The control shows one of three severities, set by the severity property (none by default, error, warning, success): its border takes the severity's accent functional border color and the message, the message property shown only with a severity, takes the severity's functional text color. A message carries every severity, in the same part; severity replaces the invalid property and message replaces errorMessage. On the web the error is aria-invalid="true" (and :user-invalid when the browser validates) and the severity is also data-severity; warning and success have no web state and are said in the message text. The fill, the icon and the message wording of each severity are rendered in Forms step 6. The accent borders reach 3:1 on every surface level since the Color foundation 7.1.0 (decision border-accent-functional-3-to-1); the light warning border is 2.95:1 on the subtle warning fill, which step 6 may use as the fill, a shortfall the team accepted knowingly (issue #119).
decisions.rationale: The team validated the Forms foundation's three severities (decision forms-validation-severities) and named the property severity; "error" is the word every platform uses (WCAG 3.3.1 Error Identification, Compose error semantics, Material error text), where "invalid" is the web's technical term. The clean break is deliberate: the packages are alpha and unreleased, and a deprecated alias would cost a schema field and support in the validator, the bridge and the templates. This amends decisions field-colors and label-description-error, whose text still says invalid and error message.

decisions.text: The control is a box on the default surface outlined in the accent neutral border color; hover tints it with the surface hover color and keeps the border; invalid takes the base error border; disabled takes the shared disabled colors. Value text is primary, the placeholder tertiary, the description secondary, the error message the error text color.
decisions.rationale: The Figma library maps no color to form controls. The accent neutral border is the lightest neutral border that keeps 3:1 against the surface in both modes (WCAG 1.4.11); the hover tint reuses the surface's own hover step.

decisions.text: Three sizes from the Figma library's space and body scales: small (32 px high, 8 px inline padding, 14 px text), medium (40, 12, 16, the default) and large (48, 16, 20); the border is 0.6 px (stroke-width.sm) and the corners 4 px (corner-radius.xs) at every size; label, description and error message keep 14 px.

A field always has a visible label above the control; help text goes under the control as the description, and the error message under it while the field is invalid. Both are exposed as the control's description.

The select is the platform's native select: the component styles the closed box and its chevron only; the opened list, its keyboard interaction and its announcements belong to the browser or the platform and are not specified here.
decisions.rationale: A custom list needs script to be accessible (focus management, arrow keys, type-ahead), and the web implementation ships none.

decisions.text: A chevron (expand_more, the icon font) sits over the end edge of the control at 16, 20 or 24 px by size, 8 px from the edge; the control reserves 28, 36 or 40 px of end padding for it. It follows the value color and is hidden from assistive technology.

changelog.note: Decision severity-fill, after the Forms decision forms-severity-fill (#105 step 12): with a severity the control takes the subtle fill of its severity (new tokens control.background.error, .warning, .success = form.control.background.<severity>) at rest and on hover alike; hover no longer tints a control in a severity. Measured: value on the fills 16.91, 17.15, 17.31:1 (light) and 11.68, 11.55, 11.43:1 (dark); border on its fill error 5.46 and 5.14:1, warning 5.87 and 8.28:1, success 7.18 and 6.17:1.

Decision form-family-aliases, after the Forms decision forms-token-family (#105 step 2b, point b6): the container gap, the label's color and font sizes, the control's fill at rest and on hover, its border in each severity and its value, the description's and the message's colors and font sizes alias the Forms family (form.*), every resolved value unchanged; its border at rest stays global.border.accent.neutral.default, where the family has the field family's global.border.base.neutral.5.

Forms decision forms-guidelines-once (#105 step 2b, point b5): the form-wide guidelines leave this specification, said once in the Forms foundation and listed on this page under "From the Forms foundation", by the tiers this control follows: the visible label, its association on the web (label element, aria-describedby), the severity in text, aria-invalid and the required attribute, the required mark (the last stale since forms-required-marking). The references only they cited are dropped. No rendering change.

Decision text-sizes (Forms forms-text-sizes, #105 step 2b, point b4): label.typography, description.typography and message.typography become one token per size (small, medium and large): the label 14 / 16 / 16 px (medium, tight line height), the description 12 / 12 / 14 px, the message 14 / 16 / 16 px (medium), all 14 px before; the size property now affects these parts. No color change.

Decision part-gap (Forms forms-part-gaps, #105 step 10, point 5): container.gap space.4 → space.6, so label, control, description and message are 6 px apart as in the Text field family. No color change.

Fix: the example's error message and the content guideline rely on the label it sits under and no longer repeat the field's name ("Choose one"), as the Forms foundation decides (forms-message-relies-on-label). No rendering change.
Fix: the examples' message and description of one sentence end with no period, as the Forms foundation decides (forms-message-punctuation). No rendering change.
Fix: the disabled property no longer advises read-only, which a select does not have: the readonly attribute is not relevant to the select element (MDN: the readonly attribute). No rendering change.

Fix, no decision of the Select changed: the Color foundation's decision border-accent-warning-600 sets the light warning border to warning 600 #765818 (was 500 #BD8107): 6.49:1 on the default surface, 6.16:1 at the lowest (was 3.27:1 and 3.09:1), 5.86:1 on the subtle warning fill. Tokens, CSS and template unchanged.

Fix, no decision of the Select changed: the Color foundation's decision warning-on-base-600 sets the warning text to warning 600 #765818 in light mode (was warning 800 #3E2D0C): message.color.warning is 6.49:1 on the default surface and 6.16:1 at the lowest (was 13.01:1 and 12.30:1); dark mode is unchanged. The tokens, CSS and template are unchanged.

Breaking, decision forms-severity: the invalid property is replaced by severity (none, error, warning, success), errorMessage by message and the part error-message by message, the state invalid by error, warning and success; the web attribute data-invalid by data-severity. Tokens: control.border-color.invalid is control.border-color.error, with warning and success and reads the accent functional border (global.border.accent.functional.<severity>.default) instead of the base error border; error-message.* is message.*, and message.color.<severity> reads global.text.on-base.functional.<severity>.default. CSS: [data-severity="<severity>"] and [data-state="<severity>"], select__error-message is select__message. The accent borders reach 3:1 on every surface level since the Color foundation 7.1.0 (decision border-accent-functional-3-to-1); the light warning border is 2.95:1 on the subtle warning fill, which step 6 may use as the fill, a shortfall the team accepted knowingly (issue #119).

Follows the Iconography foundation 0.3.0 (decision optical-size-24): the indicator glyph is drawn for optical size 24 instead of 20 (select.indicator.optical-size → font.icon.optical-size.24). Sizes and colors unchanged, so contrast is unchanged.

Fix, no decision changed: the Figma library's POC2 export (Color foundation 3.1.0) moves the values of the roles the tokens alias; the tokens, CSS and template are unchanged. Light: 7 tokens follow the ash retune (one to four units per channel); error-message.color reads global.text.on-base.functional.error.default: #E12A23 becomes #C01619. Dark: 6 tokens follow the ash retune (one to four units per channel); control.border-color.default reads global.border.accent.neutral.default: #B9B7B7 becomes #CFCFCF; control.border-color.invalid reads global.border.base.functional.error.default: #E12A23 becomes #DF2821; error-message.color reads global.text.on-base.functional.error.default: #EE5248 becomes #F88275. Contrast re-measured on the accessibility guidelines: 3.82 → 3.73:1, 4.26 → 5.79:1, 4.52 → 6.12:1, 4.97 → 7.06:1, 5.79 → 5.77:1, 11.27 → 11.28:1, 12.14 → 12.09:1, 12.80 → 12.76:1, 12.87 → 12.78:1, 19.07 → 19.03:1.

Initial draft (decisions field-colors, sizes, label-description-error, native-list, chevron-indicator). Native select in a wrapper with a label element, a chevron, a description and an error message; options as a repeated part; states default, hover, focus-visible, invalid, disabled; sizes small, medium, large. Contrast on the default surface, light / dark: label and value 19.07 / 11.27, description 12.87 / 8.80, error text 4.52 / 4.97 (4.26 on level 1 in light mode), border at rest 12.87 / 8.80 and 12.14 / 8.06 on hover, error border 6.12 / 3.82, focus ring 5.79 / 12.80.
